Heikin Ashi

Slide 29 (3:42-3:57)

to give less noise than a traditional Candlestick a green hinachi candle signals that the price is on an uptrend and a red HK kanashi candle signals that the price is on a downtrend the size of the candle's body also indicates how strong a trend is the larger the candle

Slide 30 (3:57-4:06)

the stronger the trend keep in mind that the ha kanashi only acts as an indicator it does not display the real market price moon phases it is a concept that

Smoothed candles: green = uptrend, red = downtrend, bigger body = stronger trend; less noise but not the real price. Testable as a trend or exit filter (exit when the Heikin Ashi colour flips).

Support & resistance

Slide 51 (6:21-6:33)

these are key levels that formed horizontally where the price has bounced off in the past and could possibly bounce again in the future if the level is below the Price It's called support where you can take a buy position if the

Slide 52 (6:33-6:39)

price approaches it and if the level is above the price it's called resistance where you can take a sell position if the price approaches it Dynamic support

Horizontal levels where price bounced before: buy near support, sell near resistance. This is what the swing-size study measures (bounce vs break at swing levels).

Dynamic support & resistance

Slide 54 (6:42-6:54)

resistance Dynamic support and resistance also acts as key levels but instead of using static horizontal lines it uses indicators like the moving average to act as our key level trend

Moving averages (or VWAP) acting as support in a trend. Your EMA pullback idea; testable as bounce rate at EMA 20/50 and VWAP touches.

Trend lines

Slide 56 (6:57-7:06)

form diagonally during a trend Market you can use trend lines to identify the overall direction of the price upwards trend line means bullish downwards trend

Slide 57 (7:06-7:15)

line means bearish and similar to support and resistance you can also use the trend line to identify possible entry scenarios for example if price

Slide 58 (7:15-7:21)

retraces back to a trend line it can be a good opportunity to take a buy position gone angles it is a tool that

Line through swing lows (uptrend) or highs (downtrend); a retrace to the line is a buy (or sell) opportunity. Codeable: line through the last two confirmed swing lows, touch and bounce/break stats.
